title: Make a first script and presentation
description: Create a sectioned script, open the reader, and make a calm first pass through your notes.
body:
# Make a first script and presentation

The quickest way to learn Quickque is to write a small script and present it. Scripts live on the device in the library; there is no account to create and no upload step.

## Before you begin

- Open Quickque in the browser preview or the desktop app.
- Have a short outline ready. A few sentences are enough.
- For a native presentation, use the Mac app. The browser can read manually but cannot provide native window behavior.

## Steps

1. In the library, select **New script** beside the Quickque heading. Quickque creates **Untitled Script** with **Section 1** selected.

2. Replace **Untitled Script** in the script title field with a useful title such as `Quarterly update`.

3. Replace **Section 1** with a beat of the talk, such as `Opening`, and type the words into **Type your script here...**. Keep paragraphs where you want a natural pause.

4. Select **Add Section** and give the new section a name. Add the remaining beats of the talk. Use the up and down controls on a section when the order needs changing.

5. Select **Present** in the editor header. Quickque opens the reader at the beginning of the selected script.

![Quickque library in the browser preview](/images/library.webp)

*Browser preview only: the screenshot shows the library and editor workflow; it is not evidence of native overlay behavior.*

6. In the reader, leave **Manual Scroll** selected for a first run. Select the round play button, or press **Space**, to begin. Use the section selector at the bottom to jump deliberately rather than hunting through the page.

7. Stop with the play button or **Space** when someone interrupts. The reader keeps the position marker. Resume when the conversation returns to your outline.

8. Press **Esc** when you are done. Quickque exits the reader and returns to the library.

![Quickque reader in the browser preview](/images/reader.webp)

*Browser preview only: the screenshot illustrates the reader layout, not a promise that a web page can float above Zoom or Meet.*

## Expected result

Your script is visible in the library, divided into named sections, and can be opened with **Present**. Manual playback starts and pauses without throwing away your place. Pressing **Esc** returns to the editor. The script remains in local storage for the same app origin.

## Troubleshooting

- **The library says No scripts yet:** select **New script** or **Create Script**. If an error banner appears, read it before retrying; a storage failure leaves the existing library untouched.
- **Present does nothing:** select a script in the library first, then use **Present** in the editor header. A script must have an active selection.
- **The reader is moving too quickly:** pause with **Space**, then adjust **Scroll Speed** before resuming. See [Playback, speed, and interruptions](/guide/playback/).
- **I cannot see a native floating window:** browser Compact Overlay Mode is confined to the current browser window. Use the desktop app for the Mac overlay described in [Mac overlay](/guide/mac-overlay/).
- **My changes are missing after switching devices:** browser and desktop storage are separate. Use **Settings & backups** → **Export Full Backup** in one origin and **Import Backup JSON** in the other; see [Backup, restore, and migration](/guide/backup-restore/).

Read next: [Creating and managing scripts](/guide/scripts/), [Playback](/guide/playback/), or [Backup and restore](/guide/backup-restore/).
